subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which was the last Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
explanation: The expedition to Tabuk in 9 AH was the last campaign in which the Prophet personally took part.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The army of the Tabuk expedition is known as:
explanation: It was called the Army of Hardship because it set out in intense heat, at harvest time and with scarce resources.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The expedition of Tabuk ended:
o: Without any battle with the Romans
With a major defeat of the Romans
explanation: The Byzantine army did not appear; the Prophet stayed at Tabuk, made pacts with local rulers and returned.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion was among the three who stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse and were later forgiven?
explanation: Ka’b bin Malik, Hilal bin Umayyah and Murarah bin Rabi’ were boycotted for fifty days until the Qur’an announced their forgiveness.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Masjid-e-Zirar was demolished because it was built:
o: By hypocrites to cause harm and division
explanation: The Qur’an exposed it as a mosque built by hypocrites to harm the believers, and the Prophet had it pulled down after Tabuk.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The year 9 AH is known as Aam-ul-Wufood because:
o: Many tribal delegations came to accept Islam
explanation: After the conquest of Makkah, delegations from across Arabia came to Madinah to embrace Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The invitation to Mubahala was made to a Christian delegation from:
explanation: When the Christians of Najran disputed about Isa (AS), the Prophet invited them to a mutual invocation; they chose a peace settlement.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first Hajj of the Muslims in 9 AH was led by:
explanation: The Prophet appointed Abu Bakr as Amir-ul-Hajj in 9 AH; the Prophet himself performed Hajj the next year.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hajjat-ul-Wida (the Farewell Pilgrimage) was performed in:
explanation: The Prophet performed his only Hajj after the Hijrah in 10 AH, a few months before his death.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in:
explanation: He passed away in Madinah in Rabi-ul-Awwal 11 AH (632 CE).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was buried:
o: In the chamber of Hazrat Aishah (RA)
explanation: He was buried where he passed away, in Aishah’s room adjoining the mosque, now within Masjid-e-Nabawi.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: After Badr, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) consulted Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hazrat Umar (RA) about:
o: The site of the Prophet’s Mosque
The treatment of the prisoners of war
explanation: Abu Bakr advised ransom and Umar urged severity; the Prophet accepted ransom, illustrating consultation in state decisions.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built in:
explanation: The Prophet and his Companions built the mosque soon after arriving in Madinah in the first year of the Hijrah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first Islamic state was established in:
explanation: After the Hijrah the Prophet became head of a community with its own constitution, defence and administration at Madinah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah provided for a truce between the Muslims and the Quraysh of:
explanation: The treaty fixed a ten-year truce; the Quraysh broke it within two years, leading to the conquest of Makkah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: At Khaibar, the strong fortress of Qamus was conquered under the command of:
explanation: The Prophet gave the banner to Ali, who led the assault that took Qamus.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away at the age of:
explanation: He lived sixty-three years: forty before prophethood, thirteen in Makkah and ten in Madinah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: During his final illness, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) directed that the congregational prayers be led by:
explanation: When he was too ill to come to the mosque he instructed that Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet is known by the title “Khalilullah”?
explanation: Khalilullah means “the Friend of Allah”, a title the Qur’an gives to Ibrahim (AS).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The title “Kalimullah” belongs to:
explanation: Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah, “the one who spoke with Allah”, because Allah addressed him directly at Mount Tur.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet is called “Ruhullah”?
explanation: Isa (AS), born without a father by Allah’s command, is described as a spirit from Allah, hence Ruhullah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The title “Safiullah” is given to:
explanation: Adam (AS), the first man and first prophet, is traditionally called Safiullah, “the chosen one of Allah”.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet is known as “Zabihullah”?
explanation: Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah because his father Ibrahim (AS) was commanded to sacrifice him and a ram was sent in his place.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) is also known by the name:
explanation: Yaqub (AS) was also called Israil, and his descendants are therefore known as the Bani Israil.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet is called “Zun-Nun” (the man of the fish)?
explanation: Yunus (AS) was swallowed by a great fish and prayed from its belly, so the Qur’an calls him Zun-Nun.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet was given authority over the wind and the jinn?
explanation: The Qur’an says the wind and the jinn were made subservient to Sulaiman (AS).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Iron was made soft by Allah for which Prophet?
explanation: The Qur’an says iron was made pliable for Dawud (AS), who made coats of mail.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet is best known for his patience in prolonged illness and loss?
explanation: Ayyub (AS) lost health, wealth and family yet remained patient and grateful, and the Qur’an praises his steadfastness.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Hud (AS) was sent to the people of:
explanation: Hud (AS) warned the powerful tribe of Aad, who were destroyed by a violent wind.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Salih (AS), whose she-camel was killed by his people, was sent to:
explanation: The Thamud hamstrung the she-camel given as a sign to Salih (AS) and were then destroyed.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Shuaib (AS) was sent to the people of:
explanation: Shuaib (AS) warned the people of Madyan against cheating in weights and measures.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The people of which Prophet were destroyed for their shameless immorality?
explanation: The people of Lut (AS) persisted in indecency and their towns were overturned.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Prophet interpreted the dream of the king of Egypt about seven fat and seven lean cows?
explanation: Yusuf (AS) explained the dream as seven years of plenty followed by seven of famine and was put in charge of the storehouses.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Yahya (AS) was the son of:
explanation: Zakariya (AS) prayed in old age for a son and was given Yahya (AS).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The foundations of the Ka’bah were raised by Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) together with:
explanation: The Qur’an describes Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) raising the foundations of the House and praying for its acceptance.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an describes the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as “Rahmatul-lil-Alameen”, which means:
explanation: Surah Al-Anbiya declares that he was sent as a mercy for all the worlds, not for one people alone.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was known in Makkah by the title:
explanation: Even before Islam she was called At-Tahirah, “the pure one”, for her character.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Aishah (RA) was the daughter of:
explanation: Aishah bint Abi Bakr, the daughter of Abu Bakr Siddiq, became one of the greatest scholars among the Companions.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Aishah (RA) is especially remembered for her contribution to:
o: Transmission of Hadith and Islamic jurisprudence
explanation: She narrated a large body of hadith and senior Companions consulted her on questions of law and Sunnah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Hafsah (RA), a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of:
explanation: Hafsah bint Umar married the Prophet after being widowed in 3 AH.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umm Habibah (RA), a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of:
explanation: Umm Habibah (Ramlah) embraced Islam early and emigrated to Abyssinia even while her father Abu Sufyan still opposed Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: After the death of Hazrat Khadijah (RA), the Holy Prophet (PBUH) married the widow:
explanation: Sawdah, an early Muslim widowed after returning from Abyssinia, married the Prophet in Makkah after Khadijah’s death.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was known as “Umm-ul-Masakeen” (mother of the poor)?
explanation: Zainab bint Khuzaymah was famed for feeding the poor even before Islam, and died within months of her marriage.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The last lady whom the Holy Prophet (PBUH) married was:
explanation: He married Maimunah bint al-Harith in 7 AH at the time of Umrat-ul-Qaza.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Juwayriyah (RA), whose marriage led to the release of many captives, belonged to:
explanation: She was the daughter of the chief of Banu Mustaliq; after the marriage the Companions freed her tribe’s captives as the Prophet’s in-laws.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Safiyyah (RA) was the daughter of:
o: Huyayy bin Akhtab, a chief of Banu Nadir
explanation: Safiyyah was from a leading Jewish family of Banu Nadir; she married the Prophet after Khaibar.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was married to Hazrat Ali (RA)?
explanation: Fatimah az-Zahra married Ali bin Abi Talib; she was the mother of Hasan and Husain (RA).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The eldest daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was:
explanation: Zainab was the eldest of his four daughters by Khadijah; she was married to Abul Aas bin Rabi’.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Ibrahim, the son of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) who died in infancy in Madinah, was born of:
explanation: Ibrahim was born of Mariyah in 8 AH and died as a small child; a solar eclipse that day was not, the Prophet said, due to his death.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umm Aiman (RA), who cared for the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in his childhood, was the mother of:
explanation: Umm Aiman (Barakah) married Zaid bin Harithah and bore Usama, who became a beloved young commander.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Abbasid dynasty traced its descent from the Holy Prophet’s uncle:
explanation: The Abbasids took their name from Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet’s uncle.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was:
explanation: His name was Abdullah bin Uthman (Abu Quhafah); Atiq and Siddiq were titles.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The title “Al-Farooq” was given to:
explanation: Umar was called Al-Farooq, “the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood”, after his open acceptance of Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Uthman (RA) is called “Zun-Nurain” because he:
o: Compiled two copies of the Qur’an
Married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
explanation: Zun-Nurain, “possessor of two lights”, refers to his marriages to Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum, daughters of the Prophet.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The kunyah “Abu Turab” was affectionately given by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to:
explanation: Finding Ali asleep in the mosque covered with dust, the Prophet called him Abu Turab, “father of dust”, a name Ali cherished.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion was given the title “Amin-ul-Ummah” (the trustworthy one of the Ummah)?
explanation: The Prophet said every nation has a trustworthy one and the trustworthy one of this Ummah is Abu Ubaidah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) called which Companion his “Hawari” (special disciple)?
explanation: At the Battle of the Trench the Prophet said every prophet has a disciple and his disciple is Zubair.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion is known as “Tarjuman-ul-Qur’an” (interpreter of the Qur’an)?
explanation: The Prophet prayed for Ibn Abbas to be given understanding of the religion; he became the leading early authority on Tafsir.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion is known as “Sayyid-ul-Qurra” (leader of the reciters)?
explanation: Ubayy bin Ka’b was praised by the Prophet as the best reciter; Umar appointed him to lead Taraweeh in Madinah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion is honoured with the title “Sayyid-ush-Shuhada” (chief of the martyrs)?
explanation: The Prophet’s uncle Hamza, martyred at Uhud, was given this title by the Prophet.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib (RA) is called “Tayyar” because:
o: He was granted wings in Paradise after his martyrdom at Mutah
He carried messages swiftly to Abyssinia
He led the cavalry at Khaibar
He flew a banner at Badr
explanation: After he lost both arms holding the banner at Mutah, the Prophet said Allah had given him two wings in Paradise.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The term “Ashara Mubashara” refers to:
o: Ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise
explanation: In one hadith the Prophet named ten Companions, including the four caliphs, as promised Paradise.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA) originally belonged to:
explanation: Salman was a Persian who left Zoroastrianism in search of truth, passed through Christian teachers and found Islam in Madinah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Suhaib (RA) is called “Rumi” because he:
o: Was a Roman general who converted
Grew up among the Byzantines after being captured as a child
explanation: Suhaib was an Arab captured as a boy and raised in Byzantine lands, so he spoke with a Roman accent and was called Rumi.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Abu Dhar Ghifari (RA) is best remembered for his:
o: Asceticism and outspokenness against hoarding wealth
explanation: Abu Dhar lived simply and warned the wealthy against amassing riches, a stance he maintained throughout his life.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion was the first to shoot an arrow in the way of Allah?
explanation: Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas, a skilled archer, shot the first arrow in an early expedition and later conquered Iraq.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion is known as the poet of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
explanation: Hassan bin Thabit answered the Quraysh poets in defence of the Prophet and is called Sha’ir-ur-Rasool.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Anas bin Malik (RA) is known as:
o: The personal attendant of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
The scribe of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
explanation: His mother brought him as a boy to serve the Prophet, whom he served for years in Madinah and later narrated many hadith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Mu’adh bin Jabal (RA) as governor and judge to:
explanation: Mu’adh, among the most learned Companions in matters of halal and haram, was sent to Yemen to teach and judge.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The only Companion mentioned by name in the Holy Qur’an is:
explanation: Zaid is named in Surah Al-Ahzab in the context of the rulings on adoption.
